title: Playing a society job for W. C. Handy
summary: Scott subs on a Fifth Avenue society date, takes choruses on St. Louis Blues, and Handy praises him.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Where the blues came from: Handy, Bolden and early blues

blocks.x: Now, one time, when I was working with them, I played for the fellow, W.C. Handy, that wrote the St. Louis Blues. These fellows that had come out of the Army -- and they all belonged to the Amsterdam, a guy by the name of Casco Williams, the saxophone player. He and Cecil knew each other, they had been in the band together, Jim Mueller's band. And they were short a trumpet player one time, and Cecil told him, said, Casco, why don't you get Scotty? He knows all the popular tunes, he could play.

They got me, and I was scared to death. Old Man Handy was on the job. We played down on Fifth Avenue in a millionaires house, because those days, there was nothing but millionaires that owned the places there. They hadn't torn them all down
for office buildings then. We played there -- of course, they had a big palatial place, and we were situated in the corner nice, and, oh, it was grand.

Naturally, it was befitting that they play St. Louis Blues, and them being there and all like that, we'd play it. Well, I took a chorus on St. Louis Blues myself. Somebody said, take another one. I took another one. And then we played and played and played. After we got through, we -- whatever they were serving the guests to eat, the always had somebody special to serve the band, too. We were in the corner table, always got what they got, all that fancy food and stuff. And, me, I could never afford to buy what I ate.

And Old Man Handy said, Kid Scottie -- he called me Kid Scottie -- he said, I like the way you played my number. Said, you keep up the work like that and you'll go someplace. See, that hit me, that made me feel awfully good, because there he was,the author of the St. Louis Blues. And everybody did the St Louis Blues. That was the first blues they learned how to play.
